  patch none of whose listed tiles can show draws its `PlaneMesh`), and nothing until then. So no frame shows the base ground under a graded
  road or a set with a listed tile missing. A patch whose list has not arrived draws nothing; a
  patch drawing nothing shows the background (the sky) where it lies. A set that drew complete
  keeps drawing through its patch's residency while its list is refreshed: an edit installs its
  own tiles in its batch's frame, and a tile the refreshed list adds that the edit did not select
  renders the base it rendered before, which its bake keeps. A list of an older generation (an
  edit's patch, its new list in flight) counts the set's installed tiles with it, so a commit's
  tiles keep drawing until the new list arrives. A patch drawing nothing whose list names a tile
  builds its set first, as a patch a shown tile waits for does (urgent: at least one tile a frame
  under the streaming budget). Drawing nothing is a collapsed `PlaneMesh` (the
  node stays visible for grass and the water reflection, which keep drawing there) and a hidden
  set. `has_pending_work()` counts a patch drawing nothing, so the settled signal implies none.
  - **Residency margin.** A newly resident patch is ready after its list, its tiles' bakes and
    installs and its set's build: `ready_ms_max` and `ready_frames_max` count it per patch. The
    residency already reaches past the view: patches within the cull distance (8,000 m, or four
    times the camera height) plus one patch, and two more patches before one is added or dropped
    (`PATCH_RESIDENCY_HYSTERESIS_PATCHES`), so a patch enters the residency at least 1,530 m
    beyond the cull distance along an axis, and with the game camera's far plane (9,000 m at the
    farthest zoom) at least 530 m before it can enter the view. At the fastest keyboard pan (240
    m/s scaled by the orbit distance over 400 m: 600 m/s at the farthest 1,000 m zoom), that is
    0.88 s. The margin's check is `unready_in_view`: patches drawing nothing whose culling box
    meets the camera's frustum, in any frame, recorded over the idle benchmark's camera paths
    (`pan_high` moves 10 m a frame, the fastest pan at 60 fps). It costs no memory beyond today's
    residency; the round 7 record has the measurement.
  - **The world's "ready"** (the user, 2026-10-28; the near ring by `TERRAIN-15`, the user,
    2026-10-30). A world load (`input_manager.gd`, both load paths and a new game) hands the game
    over once every patch of the world within `WORLD_READY_RADIUS_M` (2,000 m, where `GL2` ends)
    of the camera's ground point draws what it draws settled: resident, its list arrived or
    refused, and not drawing nothing (`terrain.gd`'s `unready_patches_near_camera`,
    `terrain_graded_tiles.gd`'s `unready_near`, O(patches within the radius)). Until then it takes
    no input (no camera control, no tool), the simulation clock stays stopped
    (`set_simulation_speed` refuses a running speed), and the graded work takes the whole frame
    (`terrain.gd`'s `set_load_settling`, the renderer's `unbudgeted`). From the hand-over the
    farther patches stream on within the frame budget while the player plays, each drawing
    nothing (the background) until its set draws, by the rule above; `is_render_settled()` holds
    once they are done. There is no loading screen yet: before the hand-over the screen shows what
    the renderer draws. The hand-over emits `world_ready`. A real loading screen over that wait is
    [`UI-08`](roadmap.md), not part of `TERRAIN-07`. A camera jump (a teleport, a follow) can
    still bring patches into view before they are ready: they show the background until they
    are.
- **Settled** (`TERRAIN-07-G` round 6). `terrain.gd`'s `is_render_settled()` is the one signal a
  capture of the drawn terrain and a world load's hand-over wait for: no pending patch work and
  no graded tile work (`terrain_graded_tiles.gd`'s `has_pending_work()`: tile and list requests,
  counts, results deferred past a frame's budget, an edit batch, a resident patch drawing
  nothing, and the set builds of patches a shown tile waits for or whose list names a tile; a set
  whose patch lists none stays hidden when built). The reference test, the edit probe and the
  renderer test wait on it. In every frame of the reference test's waits (each fixture streams in
  from an empty residency, and its patches change step with the camera) and of the renderer
  test, no patch draws its `PlaneMesh` where its list names a graded tile or has not arrived, or
  where a preview tile meets it (`plane_violations()`), and no set draws with a listed tile
  missing (`partial_sets()`, the renderer test outside its edits); settled, no patch draws
  nothing (`hole_patches()`). The idle benchmark records the load to settled (`load_to_settled`)
  apart from its own waits. Round 5's flipping sloped obliques were captures taken while cell
  set builds were still queued.
- **Instance uniforms.** The cells place themselves from instance uniforms (`cell_mode`, the patch
  rectangle, the lattice anchor), and Godot holds every instance's instance uniforms in one global
  buffer of `rendering/limits/global_shader_variables/buffer_size` vec4 slots, 16 per instance; an
  instance past it renders with the defaults, so a base cell collapses and its patch shows the sky
  (`TERRAIN-07-D` round 7: on Kuopio the prewarmed cell sets alone passed the default 65,536 slots,
  4,096 instances, and the game's trees had passed it before them, [`WATER-05`](roadmap.md#validated-bugs)).
  `project.godot` sets 1,048,576 slots (65,536 instances, 16 MB): twice the most a session asked
  for (the round 7 matrix's saved sessions refused 26,581 allocations past the 4,096 with the trees), the `T7` rule.
  Since round 9 only sets drawing a patch hold slots ([cell sets](#godot-tile-renderer)): with
  Godot's default buffer the saved pose refuses 43 allocations (the exact cut 6,173, round 8's
  scripts 11,387).
- **Shader.** One source with two variants, an include plus thin wrappers as the paving shaders
  have. The base variant is today's `terrain.gdshader` and has no discard, so ungraded terrain keeps
  early depth. The graded variant adds the height `base + delta` (`texelFetch` at the vertex's
  lattice point), the normal from today's base gradient plus the central difference of `delta`
  over the apron, the exact mask and the material class. Both share the grass and paving includes,
  the baked world noise (`TERRAIN-04`), the patch masks (`TERRAIN-06`), the overlays, the shoreline
  sampling of the water texture and the cloud shadow in `light()`.
  The mask and the class read a tile's rows from its page's atlas through the slot's header
  texel (round 8): row `i` at `(i & 255, first + (i >> 8))`, the edges, heights and lists at the
  header's offsets. `render_tests.rs` ports this addressing over the packed bytes, so
  `the_exact_mask_equals_coverage` and the bend and cap checks run on what the shader reads.
- **No plain cells** ([T35](#terrain-07-open-questions) (b), built in `TERRAIN-07-D` round 9,
  reverted in round 11). Drawing the tiles whose samples are none covered, named or painted with
  a variant without the mask was exact and invisible, but took 0.014 ms of the saved pose's
  0.19 ms for 41 MiB of video memory, twice the cell sets' prewarm and four more `MultiMesh`es
  and materials per set; the binding of a set's materials while it draws stays.
- **Walls.** A tile's wall faces (conflict walls, abutments, headwalls, the portal opening's
  sides) reach Godot with its slot bytes, eight little-endian `f32` per face (`pack_walls`:
  `a`, `b`, the bottoms and the tops). Each pooled cell set holds one more `MultiMesh`, of one
  quad, prewarmed with 1,024 instances; a face draws as one instance of the patch holding its
  midpoint, its eight values carried raw in the instance transform's basis (full floats in both
  renderers) and placed in world space by `terrain_graded_walls.gdshader`, which lights it
  through `standard_light.gdshaderinc` in the exact cut's retaining wall colour. Faces past the
  capacity are counted and logged. Nothing is created per edit (`TERRAIN-07-D` round 4).
- **Water reflection** ([T38](#terrain-07-open-questions) (a), `TERRAIN-07-D` round 10). The
  reflection world's terrain proxies mirror each patch's `PlaneMesh` at the shader's default
  `cell_mode`, so the mirror draws the base ground where cells draw a patch; the cells are not
  mirrored, as the roads they grade around are not.
- **Debug.** `terrain_visual_debug_mode` gains `delta` (raised orange, lowered blue, as the spike's
  `plan_grading`), `sdf`, level and slot views.

### Preview, commit, undo and load

- **Dirty tiles.** From the roadbed's terrain changes: every tile that meets a changed seam's box
  grown by its selection bound, at each level's band. The bound has the four terms of the pruning
  reach, with the ranges and the slope taken over everything within `3C` of the seam, so it is at
  least the reach of every tile whose window can hold the seam. A superset is safe: rebaking an
  unaffected tile reproduces its bits. From site changes: the old and new footprints' seams and
  surface edges likewise. From a base edit: the tiles holding its changed samples' bilinear
  support, since `g(p)` reads the base only at `p`. A stroke that re-solves road profiles
  (`ROAD-68-E` part 2) adds its roads' changes.
  Correction (`TERRAIN-07-A`, `dirty_tiles_for_road_changes`): the bound is computed per
  candidate tile, not over `3C`. The candidates are the tiles within `max(C, B)` of a changed
  segment; each takes the reach its own bake computes (its window's slope and the base under the
  segment), with the window's seam heights widened by every changed segment, so the bound holds
  before and after the change and a removed segment counts. `3C` did not contain every affected
  tile's window (a tile within `C` of the segment, 64 m wide, with a window of `C` beyond it,
  reaches `3C` plus the apron), and per-tile windows are tighter. A tile whose lattice meets a
  changed piece's bounds is dirty too when the grounded top triangles that can cover its lattice
  differ between the roadbeds before and after the change (pieces published in both with the same
  mesh skipped, the others' triangles compared as sorted bits): coverage and the road surface
  under the deep inside rule change only there, also where no chain changed, and a split trunk's
  far half, rebuilt bit for bit, marks nothing. The selection therefore reads both roadbeds; the
  preview and the commit hold the one before the edit (`O(1)` snapshots).
  Correction (`TERRAIN-07-A` round 2, with the [two-pass pruning](#the-grading-function)): a
  changed segment marks a candidate tile where the bake's pass 1 would list it in a bin of the
  tile (the same bins, base ranges and test), or where its box lies within `(h_hi - F_t) / k` of
  the lattice, `F_t` the lowest `h_lo + k D` over the window's seams of both roadbeds (`D` from a
  seam's box to the lattice): at a sample below its base the first-pass ground is at least some
  seam's upper bound `h + k d >= F_t`, so pass 2 cannot list the segment either. The round 1 bound
  used the window's Lipschitz slope and lowest seam, which on Kuopio's hills is the cap and
  selected tiles whose bits never change. `graded_stage`, which the populated and Kuopio
  benchmarks share, checks outside its timing that every `GL0` tile within the cap and band of the
  edit whose bits change is selected.
- **Preview.** `preview_road` selects the dirty tiles from the preview roadbed's changes and bakes
  the resident ones at their current level, synchronously on the shared pool, with their inputs;
  a pose bakes only the tiles whose inputs differ from the last pose's staged tiles, so a drag
  pays per pose for what the pose changed, never the whole edit ([T20](#terrain-07-open-questions)
  (a)).
  Godot uploads them into free slots and swaps the instances to them (and the cells' meshes where a
  tile becomes graded or ungraded); cancel swaps back. This replaces the refined patches in the
  terrain half of the preview and `road_terrain_preview.gd`'s patch staging.
- **Commit.** For the same tiles the commit gathers the committed inputs and compares them with the
  preview's. Matching tiles are adopted: Godot keeps the preview slots and frees the old ones.
  Others are baked by the commit. The function is total, so no terrain validation can reject a
  road; only a representation error ([T7](#terrain-07-open-questions)) or a user decision on
  [T2](#terrain-07-open-questions) could.
  Until gate E's adoption (`TERRAIN-07-D` item 5) the commit selects and bakes off the frame: the
  core journals the install with `O(1)` snapshots of the heightmap and of the roadbed before and
  after it and the sites within the selection's reach, a payload worker selects every level's
  dirty tiles from them, and Godot rebakes the ones it holds and installs them together. Site
  publications, terrain brushes and world resets are journalled likewise.
- **Undo.** The roadbed's undo swaps its pieces back (`ROAD-68-E`). The undo record keeps the
  tiles the commit replaced, as the exact cut's record kept the refined terrain entries it
  replaced (the deleted `SimulationSnapshot::refined_terrain`), and undo swaps them back: no rebake
  ([T20](#terrain-07-open-questions) (a), which takes [T9](#terrain-07-open-questions) (b));
  redo swaps likewise. A kept tile is bitwise the rebake of the restored inputs (invariant 9);
  `TERRAIN-07-E` tests that equality, and an input changed meanwhile outside the undo stack
  would make a kept tile stale, which gate E must rule out or rebake. Sites are such an input
  (`TERRAIN-07-C`): the demand pass places, redevelops and removes buildings beside a committed
  road between the commit and its undo, outside the undo stack, and a kept tile within the reach
  of such a change no longer equals the rebake. The tile's inputs hold the window's sites
  (`TileInputs::sites`, canonical order, compared exactly), so gate E can compare each kept
  tile's inputs with the current ones at undo and rebake the ones that differ, or mark the kept
  tiles a site change selects ([`dirty_tiles_for_site_changes`](#sites-pads-and-paving)) stale
  as the change publishes; the second keeps undo free of input gathers.
- **Load.** No terrain surface state is saved. Tiles are baked as residency requests them.
- **Bitwise.** A preview tile equals the committed tile, a fresh bake of the same inputs, the tile
  after undo and redo, and the tile after save and load.
- **Corrections (`TERRAIN-07-E` round 1, built; [record](#terrain-07-e-record)).**
  - *One staging rule.* A pose, the commit and undo each select their dirty tiles and stage them
    against held tiles (`graded::stage_tiles`): each wanted tile's inputs are gathered without
    sampling (`tile_inputs`, the bake's own gathers and assembly), a held tile at the same level
    with equal inputs is adopted, the rest are baked. The held tiles are the last pose's for a
    pose, the current preview's for the commit and the kept tiles for undo.
  - *Where the kept tiles come from.* Rust holds no copy of a resident tile (invariant 2), so it
    has no replaced tile to keep at the commit. The undo record's kept tiles are baked from the
    pre-commit inputs by a pure job on the background pool after the commit (the roadbed and the
    heightmap before it in `O(1)`, the sites of the tiles' windows copied), never in the commit's
    frame. The inputs are taken at the commit's graded stage, but the commit queues the job only
    after its last stage, beside its lot plan and routing rebuild (`ROAD-68-G` part 10,
    [`roads.md`](roads.md#road-68-g--commit-consequences-inside-one-frame)): the two pools share
    the CPUs, and a bake queued at the graded stage took the cores of the commit's later stages.
    Undo adopts the kept tiles whose inputs equal the restored ones and bakes the rest,
    so a site the demand pass placed meanwhile, or a job not yet finished, costs a bake, never a
    stale tile; undo never waits for the job (no pool worker waits for a pure job). The simulation
    has no redo; a commit of the same stroke after undo stands for it in the tests.
  - *No terrain validation.* The commit refuses only field and cell overlaps and failed node
    pieces; a tile the payload cannot represent (`T7`) is reported with the staged tiles and
    refuses nothing.
  - *Residency in the Rust half.* Until the Godot half supplies the resident tiles and their
    levels, every dirty tile is staged at `GL0`, the dearest level and the one the budgets were
    measured at.
  - *A drag reuses almost nothing.* A growing stroke rebuilds its whole span each pose, so the
    tiles a pose selects all hold new seams: [T27](#terrain-07-open-questions).
- **Corrections (`TERRAIN-07-E` round 4, [T27](#terrain-07-open-questions) (d), decided by the
  user, 2026-10-27; built in the Rust half).**
  - *A frame stages a bounded share.* A pose's frame selects the pose's dirty tiles (`W`) and
    stages the first one of them in the pose's order; a frame without a new pose (a catch-up
    frame, `advance_road_preview_terrain`) stages the next two (three until `TERRAIN-07-G` round
    7, re-measured with T48 (a) and T49 (c) in the bake: three took 2.99-3.01 ms). The order is fixed from the
    inputs: the squared distance from the stroke's moving end (its last point) to the tile's
    square, then `(level, tile)`. Staging is the one rule above: a tile is gathered, adopted from
    the shown tiles when its inputs equal the pose's, else baked. The bounds are tile counts,
    never a clock, measured to fit 3.0 ms on four workers (`GradedPreview`, `POSE_FRAME_TILES`
    and `CATCH_UP_FRAME_TILES`): a single steep tile at a stroke's end bakes in 2.3-2.5 ms alone
    (5.3 ms on one worker), so beside the selection a pose frame fits only with one (round 4's
    measurement; round 7's in the [record](#terrain-07-g-record)).
  - *What shows.* After each frame the preview shows, for each tile of `W`, its exact bake of
    this pose's inputs once staged, else the tile an earlier pose showed, else the published
    tile; a tile outside `W` shows the published tile. Every shown tile is the exact bake of
    some pose's inputs (no blend, no fallback, no partial tile), and the shown tiles after each
    frame depend only on the sequence of poses and frames, never on timing or the worker count.
    A newer pose (or a pose without pieces, or a publication) supersedes the older pose's
    unstaged tiles; the shown tiles stay for adoption. **What the renderer draws** (`TERRAIN-12`,
    [T60](#terrain-07-open-questions) (a), the user, 2026-10-29; `ROAD-68-H` round 4): only tiles
    exact for the latest pose. An earlier pose's tile discards that pose's road footprint, so
    until round 4 the background showed where the new pose's road did not cover it, and a pose
    without pieces kept the earlier tiles drawn while the road tool drew no road. Now an unstaged
    tile of `W` keeps an earlier pose's tile only where the move from the latest pose left its
    inputs unchanged (a second selection, of the move), else the published tile draws until it
    is staged; a pose that draws no road (no pieces, or invalid) and a publication draw no
    preview terrain. The adoption pool above is unchanged, so every staged, committed and undone
    tile is too. `TERRAIN-12` is done (`ROAD-68-H` round 6) for the hole classes this and T61 fix
    (the corridors, the seam cracks, the undo's frame); a pose that rebuilds an existing road's
    pieces (a junction) still shows the background where the published tiles cut the replaced
    pieces until its selection displays, and a fast click's newly graded tile waits for its
    patch's list beside an installed one: both carried to [T65](#terrain-07-open-questions)
    (the user, 2026-10-29), not accepted.
  - *Convergence.* Once the poses stop, the shown tiles are the last pose's after
    `ceil((|W| - 1) / 2)` catch-up frames, bitwise its fresh bake and the commit's tiles.
  - *The commit.* The click offers the tiles the preview shows at that moment (the latest
    preview's, updated by each catch-up frame); the commit adopts those whose inputs match and
    bakes the rest in its own frame, so the committed tiles are exact at once. A click right
    after a fast drag finds most of `W` unstaged and bakes it: that stage can exceed 3.0 ms
    ([T27](#terrain-07-open-questions) (f), accepted by the user, 2026-10-27); it is never
    spread over frames.
  - *What stays exact.* The preview's road surface, markings and junctions every frame; the
    commit, undo and load bitwise in the frame they happen. Cancel swaps back to the published
    tiles as before.
- **Corrections (`TERRAIN-07-E` round 5, the Godot half; [record](#terrain-07-e-record)).**
  - *Levels* ([T42](#terrain-07-open-questions), taken pending the user's review,
    2026-10-27). The preview and the commit stage each dirty tile at the level the renderer's
    distance rule gives it from the camera (`LevelRule`: the renderer's level ends and `GL3`
    step ends, set by `set_road_preview_terrain_view` when the camera moves), without the
    hysteresis the renderer keeps around a held tile's level. The selection runs at each level
    some candidate tile may take (the levels whose distance interval meets the edit's
    candidate extent) over the candidates the rule gives that level, so each candidate is
    tested once, at its own level: `O(one selection)`. A pose's pending tiles keep the levels
    they were selected at; a commit stages by its preview's rule and undo by its commit's.
    Without a renderer (tests, benchmarks) every tile stays at `GL0`, as the budgets were
    measured. This replaces round 1's *Residency in the Rust half*.
  - *The frames' tiles reach Godot.* `preview_road` and `advance_road_preview_terrain` return
    the frame's changed shown tiles (`graded_tiles`, packed as the residency poll's tiles, the
    token the preview epoch) and the tiles shown no more (`graded_removed`). The graded
    renderer draws a shown tile from a free slot of its level's pool in place of the installed
    tile (`show_preview`, the preview layer; the installed tiles and residency are untouched) and
    a removed one returns to the installed tile, in the same frame as the road chunks.
  - *Epochs.* `release_road_preview_terrain` ends the preview's epoch at a click (the commit
    adopts that epoch's shown tiles) or at cancel (the road tool drops that epoch's tiles); the
    next poses send theirs under the next epoch, from no shown tiles.
  - *The commit's tiles install, the journal does not rebake them.* A commit's or undo's
    staged tiles, staged for a renderer's view, ride on the edit journal's record of the install
    (`GradedInstallTiles`, with the adopted preview epoch); the edit worker packs them beside
    the edit's selection. Godot installs them in the edit's batch instead of rebaking them; the
    journal's other dirty held tiles (another level, or outside the commit's selection) rebake
    as before, and the batch installs together. The batch's frame releases the preview tiles of
    every epoch up to the commit's, so no frame shows neither. A staged tile Godot neither holds
    nor wants installs only where the preview shows it graded; its patch's list, refreshed with
    the edit's patch generations, then wants it; any other waits for that list. A commit
    without a preview (no renderer view) attaches nothing and the journal rebakes as gate D
    built it.
  - *Retired.* The exact cut's preview patches (`RoadPreviewPieces::terrain`,
    `build_road_preview_terrain`, `RoadPreviewTimes::terrain_ms`) and `road_terrain_preview.gd`,
    with the road tool view's per-patch refined entries, ledgers and site ownership (only they
    read them; the view keeps the sites the graded preview reads). A pose no longer pays
    `terrain_ms`.
  - *Sampling bands.* A tile's sampling runs in bands of four lattice rows (was 16): a steep
    tile's dear samples lie in a few rows near the road, and finer bands spread them over the
    workers. The bytes do not depend on the band height (every sample is its own and the counts
    are integers).
- **Corrections (`TERRAIN-07-E` round 6, the real display; [record](#terrain-07-e-record)).**
  - *The commit takes over the preview's slots.* Rust flags each staged commit tile whose
    payload is the one the preview showed (`adopted`: the same payload as the epoch's shown tile,
    which the renderer holds). Godot moves that tile's preview slot to the installed tile in the
    batch: nothing is uploaded and nothing drawn changes, so neither its instance nor its walls
    are rewritten. A converged commit so uploads none of its tiles; the tiles an older pose
    showed (a click right after a fast drag) still upload in the batch. A click that previews a
    pose of its own shows that pose's tiles before it commits, so the renderer holds what the
    commit adopts.
  - *No cell set is built in an edit's or a preview's frame* ([cell sets](#godot-tile-renderer)).

### Queries for consumers

Read-only, allocation-free methods on the simulation core. A point query is one chunk lookup for
the road, one site chunk lookup and the seams near the point
([T8](#terrain-07-open-questions)):

| Query | Answer | Replaces | Consumers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `base_height_at(x, z)` | the base `b(p)` | `sample_height_world`, `get_height_at_internal` | terrain brushes and authoring tools, water depth ([T13](#terrain-07-open-questions)) |
| `ground_height_at(x, z)` | the graded ground: `GL0` values (base plus the packed `f32` delta) on the `GL0` triangle under `p`, each lattice cell split along its `(i, j)`-`(i + 1, j + 1)` diagonal, which the `TERRAIN-07-D` mesh follows; at a pad the pad; in a 64 m tile without a seam or pad within the cap the bilinear base, as `raycast_surface` marches it (correction, `TERRAIN-07-D` round 2: the two queries disagreed there by the `GL0` triangles' chord of the bilinear base, 3.7 mm at the grade breaks of `vehicle_ground_support_test.gd`); under a road the hidden inside-rule surface, so callers test `mask_at` first | `sample_visual_height_world`, `raycast_visual_terrain`'s heights | generated vegetation, grass, mist, water reflection, building render probes |
| `surface_height_at(x, z)` | the visible surface: the road's `height_at` where covered, else `ground_height_at` | `get_world_surface_height_internal` and `_near` (road, site, CDT ground, visual terrain) | agents off lane, vehicle contacts, authored plants, picking, cell zoning overlays, Godot tools |
| `normal_at(x, z)` | the rendered `GL0` normal: per lattice point today's base gradient (the central difference of the base over one base cell either side) plus the central difference of the packed delta over its four neighbours, interpolated over the `GL0` triangle; the shader computes the same (correction, `TERRAIN-07-D`: the base term was the 0.5 m difference, which the [renderer rule](#godot-tile-renderer) does not draw and which would crease the shading at every graded cell's border with a base cell) | (new) | vegetation slope tests |
| `mask_at(x, z)` | `GroundClass { Natural, Graded, Road, Pad, Paved(material) }`; `Road` also where a portal opening cuts the ground (T22 5 (a)) | water's road-clip suppression, `sample_building_site_height(..).is_some()` tests, the CDT holes the grass mask rasterizes | vegetation clearance, GPU grass, water mesh cells, fields |
| `raycast_surface(origin, dir)` | the nearer of the road's ray hit and the ground hit (a base heightfield march, refined to `GL0` cells inside graded tiles), never ground a road covers or a portal opening cuts | `intersect_world_surface_internal`, `raycast_engineered_ground` | cursor, picking, tools |
| `raycast_base(origin, dir)` | the authored base | `intersect_terrain_internal` | terrain brushes |

Godot's `get_world_surface_height` and `intersect_world_surface` answer from `surface_height_at` and
`raycast_surface` since `TERRAIN-07-D` round 2; since `TERRAIN-07-F` they go through
`get_world_surface_height_internal` and `intersect_world_surface_internal`, which read the graded
surface for every Rust consumer too, after the Godot entry points ready the site index.

`Graded` means `delta != 0` outside footprints. Consumer caches keep keying on the existing
per-patch terrain payload generations, which the dirty tile selection bumps for the patches
holding dirty tiles. A gather variant collects the seams once for clustered points, as
`gather_nearby_sites` does for a vehicle's contacts (`SIM-02-K`).

### Complexity bounds

| Stage | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Window gather | `O(P + S log S)`: pieces `P` meeting the window on the 32 m grid and their `S` chain segments sorted by key, plus the sites of the 512 m site chunks |
| Per-tile bounds | `O(S + c)` for `c` base cells in the window (at most about 20 × 20 at 10 m) |
| Coverage | `O(T + K)`: top triangles `T` meeting the tile, candidate lattice points `K` in their boxes |
| Sample | `O(k)` for the `k` seams in its 4 m bin |
| Tile bake | `O(N + sum over bins of k × samples in the bin)` for `N` lattice points |
| Dirty selection | `O(changed seams × tiles within C of each)` |
| Point query | `O(P + S)` for the gather, then `O(S)` for each of three lattice points ([T8](#terrain-07-open-questions)) |
| Raycast | `O(base cells crossed + GL0 cells crossed inside graded tiles × k)` |
| Godot install | `O(dirty tiles × slot bytes)` uploads and `O(cells of changed patches)` instance writes |

No stage scans the city.

### Budgets

| Stage | Budget |
| --- | --- |
| Terrain stage per preview pose: selection, bake, pack, four workers | 3.0 ms ([`roads.md` stage budgets](roads.md#stage-budgets)), flat from 0 to 100k; under [T27](#terrain-07-open-questions) (d) per frame: a pose's selection with its share, or a catch-up frame's share |
| Terrain stage per commit (the last pose's matching tiles adopted, the rest baked) and per undo (the kept tiles swapped back, no bake), four workers | 3.0 ms, flat from 0 to 100k ([T20](#terrain-07-open-questions) (a): no frame path bakes a whole edit; the pose row is the tiles changed since the last pose) |
| Godot terrain install per pose, commit or undo | within `ROAD-68`'s 2.0 ms Godot stage and install; proposed share 1.0 ms |
| Streaming installs | 1.0 ms of the main thread per frame |
| Idle GPU frame | not above the exact cut's terrain in the same session, on the idle-frame matrix |
| Load | not above the exact cut's load in the same session (Kuopio and the populated city) |
| Memory | the pools of the [memory table](#data), plus the undo records' kept tiles ([T20](#terrain-07-open-questions)); Rust keeps no other baked tile at rest |

Accepted exception to the commit row ([T27](#terrain-07-open-questions) (f), the user,
2026-10-27): a click right after a fast drag, before the preview has caught up, bakes the tiles
the preview has not staged in its own frame, and that terrain stage may exceed 3.0 ms (measured
up to 4.72 ms on Kuopio and 4.38 ms at 100k). Its limit case, a commit with no preview before
it (no tile staged; [T43](#terrain-07-open-questions) (a), the user, 2026-10-27), may do the
same (3.5 ms at 10k and 4.3 ms at 100k on the breakdown's first samples). The commit stays
exact in its frame, `ROAD-68`'s click-to-committed under 16.7 ms stays binding, and the row's
3.0 ms holds for every other commit and undo.

Accepted by the user, 2026-10-27: the GPU and frame cost of the background cell-set builds in
the seconds after a load ([`TERRAIN-07-E` round 7](#terrain-07-e-record)). The renderer builds
every resident patch's cell set off the frame paths within the streaming budget's spare time:
on Kuopio 1,296 sets, which take about 1,070 frames (3.1 s uncapped, about 4,900 frames and 82 s
at 60 Hz) after the load's settle; inside that window a frame takes 1.4-1.5 ms more and the
viewport's GPU time 0.7-0.9 ms more on Kuopio's `close` and `overview` poses. The idle-frame row
is judged on the steady state: the matrix samples once no build is left
(`idle_frame_benchmark.gd`), and there the graded terrain costs what the exact cut does.

The spike's 1.64-2.52 ms per edit has none of: the conflict terms of the reach, coverage
rasterization, sites, materials, the apron, the levels or packing. `TERRAIN-07-A`, `-C` and `-E`
measure them against this budget; the budget is not relaxed to fit.

### Guardrails

- **Size.** No line limit. Each gate records the production lines of `simulation/terrain/graded/`
  and of the Godot renderer, tests excluded; `TERRAIN-07-G` records the legacy lines deleted.
- **No stage caches** ([invariant 2](#invariants)).
- **No hot-path allocation.** Per-worker bake scratch (bins, coverage bitset, sample buffers) and
  payload buffers are reused; Godot rewrites pooled `Image`s.
- **No second implementation.** The shader's nearest-seam order, side test and class rule mirror
  Rust's; a Rust test ports the shader's arithmetic and checks it against the bake, as
  `TERRAIN-06` mirrors the shader's mask sampling.
- **Rayon** only through `crate::thread_pools`.
- **Benchmarks gate performance.** Every gate that touches the bake, the selection, the queries or
  the install reruns its benchmark: release, pinned to P-cores, no overlapping builds or
  benchmarks, against a same-session control binary.
- **Non-repair.** The [rendering non-repair rule](#14-terrain-site-ground-water-and-lighting-materials-are-runtime-presentation)
  holds: the mask is the footprint itself, evaluated exactly, and must not hide missing roadbed
  topology. A failed node shows terrain in its gap, because coverage is pointwise.

### Implementation plan

Gates are sequential unless noted. Every gate ends with:

- a commit that compiles and adds no Clippy warning to the baseline set (the warning set compared,
  not only the count)
- its own tests passing, plus `cargo test --lib` in debug and `./run.sh --test`
- the line counts of the [guardrails](#guardrails)
- updates to this section, [`roadmap.md`](roadmap.md) and [`project.md`](project.md)

A test that cannot pass until a later gate is marked `#[ignore = "TERRAIN-07-<gate>: <reason>"]`
and listed under that gate; at `TERRAIN-07-G` none may remain. As under `ROAD-68`, the game may
break between gates (user, 2026-10-25), and the exact cut stays buildable and renderable for comparison
until `TERRAIN-07-G` deletes it ([T10](#terrain-07-open-questions)).

#### `TERRAIN-07-A` — grading core and queries, roads only

1. `simulation/terrain/graded.rs` as the API router, with `seams`, `grade`, `coverage`, `sample`,
   `tile`, `select` and `query` modules in `simulation/terrain/graded/` (round 2 added `prune`, the
   two-pass pruning's bins and lists, which the bake and the selection share).
2. Roadbed accessors, no new geometry: the grounded seams of the pieces in a rectangle, sorted by
   key; their top triangles and the coverage predicate; `take_terrain_changes` returning the
   changed segments.
3. The pointwise function for the `Road` and `Ground` classes with exact pruning; the four level
   lattices with apron; packing to texels and rows; payload inputs.
4. The queries of [queries for consumers](#queries-for-consumers) for roads, used by no consumer
   yet.
5. Benchmarks: `benchmark_graded_tiles` (the reference fixtures' 16 tiles, every level); a
   `graded_tiles` row in `benchmark_populated_commit_breakdown` after each exact-cut commit, whose
   `surface_ms` is the same-run control; a point-query benchmark.

Acceptance:

- the overlap rule is order-free and continuous; the pruned evaluation equals the evaluation over
  every seam within the cap, bitwise, on fixtures with conflicts (two footprints closer than 1:2
  allows), for batches of 1 and 16 tiles, reversed tile order, and 1, 4 and 8 workers
- neighbouring tiles' shared border samples, and every level's samples at shared lattice points,
  are bitwise equal
- coverage equals `height_at(p).is_some()` at every lattice point of every reference fixture tile
- removing a node piece (a failed node's gap) uncovers the gap and changes the mask elsewhere only
  within two texels of the open chain ends; no other region changes side (the spike's `t_cutfill`
  failure)
- across a straight edge the `GL0` triangles pass through the seam height
- the terrain stage of the populated edits at 2k, 10k, 30k and 100k is at most 3.0 ms on four
  workers, and with the edited neighbourhood fixed it stays flat from 0 to 100k with bitwise
  equal local tiles
- Kuopio, the hilly reference world (added by the coordinator's ruling of 2026-10-25: the budget
  applies to the game, and the populated city is flat, so its edits hid the conflict terms' cost,
  T18), on the reference network re-recorded with today's code under the 1:3 grade limit
  ([`roads.md` open questions 37 and 38](roads.md#road-68-open-questions); the old save's edits
  are rounds 2 and 3's evidence): `kuopio_12`'s strokes, replayed after every other case, keep
  their tiles and bits; and the full-edit terrain stage (selection plus the `GL0` bake) of every
  edit of `benchmark_kuopio_graded_edits` on four workers (each recorded stroke of
  `placements.json` on the source world, a T up a hillside and a removal on the reference save),
  with the undo record's memory per edit, is recorded as evidence. Changed by
  [T20](#terrain-07-open-questions) (a) (decided by the coordinator under the user's delegation,
  2026-10-25 night, for review): no frame path bakes a whole edit (poses bake what changed since
  the last pose, the commit adopts the last pose's tiles, undo swaps the kept tiles back), so the
  3.0 ms acceptance of those frame paths on Kuopio moves to
  [`TERRAIN-07-E`](#terrain-07-e--preview-commit-undo-and-load), which builds them; gate A builds
  none. The budget is never relaxed.
- recorded for [T1](#terrain-07-open-questions), [T2](#terrain-07-open-questions),
  [T7](#terrain-07-open-questions) and [T8](#terrain-07-open-questions): reach and seams per sample
  with the conflict terms; conflict samples within one texel of a road seam on the populated
  fixtures and Kuopio; the largest seam and edge counts per tile and level; point-query cost

#### `TERRAIN-07-A` record

Round 1, 2026-10-25, on branch `terrain07-A` (from `road` at `4dc466fc`); fresh runs on that
branch, kept apart from the spike's historical numbers above. Acceptance passed on the midpoint
rule; T2's decision changed the rule afterwards (below). Round 2 (at the end of this record)
reruns on the final rule and adds Kuopio's edits to the acceptance.

**What landed.**

- `simulation/terrain/graded.rs` (router) with `seams`, `grade`, `coverage`, `sample`, `tile`,
  `select` and `query` in `simulation/terrain/graded/`: the pointwise function for `Road` and
  `Ground` with exact pruning (4 m bins, the four-term reach per tile window), the four level
  lattices with apron (`GL3`: the tile's sides, the base step lines between them and the step line
  beyond each side), packing into RGBAF texels and seam rows (the material word is 0 until
  `TERRAIN-07-C`), the payload inputs (seam keys, the visited top triangles' bits, the base
  revisions of the 512 m chunks under the window), the typed `BakeError::SeamCapacity`, dirty tile
  selection for road changes and base edits, and the queries `base_height_at`,
  `ground_height_at`, `surface_height_at`, `normal_at`, `mask_at`, `raycast_surface` and
  `raycast_base` on `GradedSurface`. Bakes run on the shared pool with one scratch per worker;
  nothing is cached and no consumer reads any of it.
- Roadbed accessors (no new geometry): `grounded_seams_in_bounds` (sorted by key) and its unsorted
  visitor, `grounded_pieces_in_bounds`, `for_each_grounded_top_triangle_in_bounds`, and
  `top_triangle_height_at` (the predicate `height_at` uses); `TerrainChanges::segments`, the
  changed grounded chain segments themselves. `SimCore` keeps the last install's terrain changes
  for the benchmark (`TERRAIN-07-E` consumes them).
- Corrections recorded at their rules: the inside rule's depth limit
  ([the grading function](#the-grading-function), item 7), coverage from grounded pieces only
  ([inside and outside](#inside-and-outside-from-the-roadbeds-top-triangles)), dirty tiles per
  candidate tile with a covering-triangle comparison for changed pieces
  ([preview, commit, undo and load](#preview-commit-undo-and-load)), the payload's triangle inputs,
  the `GL0` triangulation and normal the queries define for `TERRAIN-07-D`
  ([queries](#queries-for-consumers)), and the row capacities ([data](#data), `T7`).
- Lines (production, tests excluded): `graded/` 1,880 (`graded.rs` 27, `coverage` 104, `grade`
  114, `query` 529, `sample` 218, `seams` 135, `select` 245, `tile` 508); tests 712 more. Roadbed

**Measurements for the open questions** (midpoint-rule build).

- **T1** (reach and seams per sample with the conflict terms): reference fixtures mean reach
  0.2-4.6 m, max 0.2-8.7 m, 0.28-0.86 candidate seams per `GL0` sample; `conflict_8` mean 22.3 m,
  max 25.0 m, 10.6 per sample. Populated commits: reach at most 0.24 m, 0.76-1.43 per sample.
  Kuopio (every road tile of the reference save): the reach reaches the cap and a `GL0` sample has
  57 candidate seams, about 5.4 ms per tile on one worker (517 tiles in 0.70 s on four), so a hilly
  edit misses the 3.0 ms stage ([T18](#terrain-07-open-questions), open).
- **T2** (conflict samples, before the decision): none in the populated city (flat) at any tier.
  Kuopio `GL0`: 78,191 conflict samples in 216 graded tiles, 1,023 of them within one texel
  (0.5 m) of a road seam; `GL1` 20,520 and 527 within 1 m. Decided since: (c), walls. The wall
  census (`wall_sites`: road seams sampled every 0.5 m, the samples with `g > h`, their total
  length, the height histogram and maximum, and the five worst sites by wall height with their
  pieces, height difference, distance, each edge's wall and sample count) runs in the populated
  benchmark (`GRADED_WALLS`) and in `kuopio_wall_sites`, which with `METRUM_CONFLICT_DUMP_DIR` also
  writes each site's `GL0` samples, seams and top triangles for renders; its results are in the
  handoff when they ran.
- **T7** (largest seam rows per tile): `GL0` 86 on the reference fixtures, 245 in the 100k city,
  233 on Kuopio; `GL1` 88 and 221 (Kuopio); `GL2` 120 (reference fixtures; not measured at city
  scale); `GL3` at step 2: 37. Windows hold up to 808 seams in the city and 1,165 on Kuopio. The
  capacities are now at least twice these ([data](#data)); edges arrive with `TERRAIN-07-C`. The
  larger rows grow the [memory table](#data)'s `GL3` pool from about 83 MB to about 150 MB (its
  rows then outweigh its texels); `TERRAIN-07-D` sizes the pools, and T7 (b), a shared row buffer,
  fits `GL3` best.
- **T8** (point-query cost): above. One gather of the seams within the cap dominates, then every
  gathered seam per lattice point; at 10 µs a query, per-agent per-frame use does not scale
  ([T19](#terrain-07-open-questions), open).

    piece seam lies at 105.5 m, 22.6 m *below* the 128.0 m ground, while the first span runs
    27-33 m *above* the flat ground (base 127-128 m), so the span 11.9 m away stands 49.9 m (site

    within 6 m (grade 4.56; edge 14: 132.8 to 156.5 m, grade 3.99) and stay on a 27-33 m
    embankment towards node 20 (171.7 m). That is a `ROAD-68` profile and node plane defect
    of the reference save (an elevated road with no structure, and a cap below the ground), not
    two roads crossing; the wall is its symptom.

    segment (21.6 and 18.9 m of height).

    cone stands 6.35 m over its lower edge. A road steeper than 1:2 always walls itself under
    TD7 (`h + γ d - k d > h` for grade `γ > k`), as a cut switchback would.

**Round 3** (2026-10-25, branch `terrain07-A` rebased onto `road` at `4710f59b`; fresh runs, kept
apart from rounds 1 and 2). Work in progress: Kuopio's edits still miss the 3.0 ms stage, and gate
A's Kuopio acceptance is judged on the re-recorded reference
([`roads.md` open question 38](roads.md#road-68-open-questions)), so the gate stays open.

- **What changed** ([the grading function](#the-grading-function)): bins of `max(4 m, spacing)`,
  so `GL3` bins at its spacing; the per-sample early exit on the value (`g = max(L, min(b, U))`
  and the nearest seam, the nearest seam alone under a road) instead of on final `L` and `U`;
  lanes of four points of a bin row (`Seam::at_lanes`, `evaluate_lanes`, the one-point
  evaluation being one lane); base stops and bin columns once per lattice column; and in the
  roadbed accessor `for_each_grounded_top_triangle_in_bounds`, a piece inside the bounds visits
  its top triangles once each instead of once per grid cell (the same set; coverage takes the
  maximum and the inputs are sorted and unique).
- **Exactness** (debug library tests, fresh, on the round 3 code before the rebase onto `4710f59b`;
  76 passed, 7 ignored with the roadbed tests): pruned equals unpruned bitwise at `GL0`, `GL2` and
  now `GL3` (step 2) on the conflict fixtures and Kuopio's edge 43 block, in batches of 16 and 1,
  reversed, on 1, 4 and 8 workers; the lanes equal one point at a time (texels, rows, inputs and
  every `BakeStats` field) on all seven fixtures at all four levels
  (`lanes_equal_one_point_at_a_time_on_every_fixture_and_level`) and on all 517 Kuopio road tiles at
  `GL0` (in `kuopio_pruned_bake_equals_every_seam`);
  `a_seam_in_lanes_equals_the_seam_at_each_point`.
- **Did round 1 under-select the 100k edit?** No. Round 1's rule (the four-term one-pass reach of
  `71601ca5`'s `reached` plus the unchanged covering-triangle half), run on today's edits with
  the coverage check (a temporary diagnostic, not committed): on the 100k city it selects the same
  13, 10 and 7 tiles as round 2 and misses none of the 12, 6 and 5 tiles whose bits change; on the
  44 Kuopio edits it selects 1,057 tiles against round 2's 476 and misses none of the 410 changed.
  The 100k edit grew with the rebase instead: 464 changed segments (round 1: 386) and the same 36
  pieces.
- **Where the stage goes** (diagnostic build with per-phase timers, four workers, the machine
  shared, untimed; CPU time summed over the 44 Kuopio edits): sampling 64 %, coverage
  rasterization 22 %, first-pass listing 5 %, list building, bins, rows, gather, base window and
  second pass 1-2 % each. Junction-heavy edits spend up to 37 % in rasterization (`kuopio_12`
  attempt 36: 5.0 of 13.5 ms). The bake's wall time is a median 1.34 times its CPU time over four
  workers (13 tiles on four workers leave the last worker four), and even a perfect split misses
  on the worst edits: `kuopio_04` attempt 10 has 16.0 ms of CPU for 13 tiles (4.0 ms over four
  workers before its 0.4 ms selection).
- **Lanes on this target.** `x86-64-v2` has two `f64` per register; LLVM vectorizes part of the
  lane arithmetic (7 `divpd` and 6 `sqrtpd` beside 21 `divsd` and 16 `sqrtsd` in `bake_tile`). The
  value exit took Kuopio's evaluated seams per sample from 2.43 to 1.86 (census) and `kuopio_04`
  attempt 10's from 7.63 to 5.74.

#### `TERRAIN-07-B` — road skirts in the piece mesh

1. `PieceMesh` gains a skirt layer: one strip per grounded outer chain, top vertices the chain's,
   0.5 m deep, with the bottom-vertex attribute.
2. The chunk emission carries the layer; the road shader draws it and deepens the bottom vertices
   by the distance rule of [T5](#terrain-07-open-questions).
3. Bridge fascias: `ROAD-68-F` part 2 found a bridge deck's sides open between the deck edge and
   the concrete slab of `standard_surface/bridge.rs` (visible from the side). The piece closes them
   with a side strip from the deck's outer edge down to the slab's top edge, from the same
   sections, so the slab and the strip share their vertices.

Acceptance: skirt tops are bitwise the chain vertices; fascia strips are watertight against the
deck edge and the slab (the `road_families` chunk check, extended);
`reference_junction_road_chunks_are_watertight` covers the skirts' top edges against the sidewalk
outer edge; previewed chunks with skirts equal the committed chunks
(`preview_chunks_with_crossings_and_signs_are_the_committed_chunks` and
`road_junction_preview_test.gd`); payload packing stays within its 1.0 ms budget
(`benchmark_road_preview_stages`); the `roadbed/` line count is recorded.

**Gate record (2026-10-25, branch `terrain07-B`).**

- **Strips in the piece mesh.** `PieceMesh` keeps the kind of strips its outer chains hang
  (`StripKind`): `Skirt` on node pieces and standard spans, `Fascia` on bridge spans, none on
  tunnels, set where the piece is built (`build_span_piece` from the edge class, as the span's
  `grounded` flag; node pieces always, as `terrain_loops` and the terrain changes count them).
  `PieceMesh::for_each_strip_triangle` constructs the strips from the chains: two triangles per
  chain segment, top points the chain's positions bitwise, bottoms `StripKind::bottom` (straight
  down by `SKIRT_DEPTH_M` 0.5 m or `BRIDGE_DECK_DEPTH_M` 0.35 m), wound to face away from the
  road, with a bottom flag per point. Nothing else is stored, so a piece costs no memory for its
  strips; there is no boolean, clip or repair, and queries never see strips (the piece grid holds
  top triangles only).
- **Chunk emission and shader.** Skirts go to payload layer 0, which was reserved for road-owned
  earthwork and never written since `ROAD-68-A`, renamed `skirt` (Rust fields, the Godot
  dictionary keys, the chunk renderer and its tests and benchmark): the curb colour, exact
  normals, and UV `y` as the bottom-vertex attribute (1 at bottoms, 0 on the chain, interpolated
  at chunk-line clip points). They pass the same chunk router and owner splice as every layer,
  so a preview's skirts are its commit's. Godot draws the layer with
  `WorldMaterials.road_skirt_material()`: the curb-face shader (`road_sidewalk_face.gdshader`)
  with `skirt` set, whose vertex stage lowers a bottom by the T5 depth minus the 0.5 m it already
  has (0.5 m to 2 km, 2.5 m to 5 km, 5 m to 12 km, 10 m beyond), with the camera distance measured
  as `terrain.gd` measures patch LOD (camera to point; a patch measures to its centre, so a skirt
  vertex can switch up to a patch half-diagonal before the patch under it: `TERRAIN-07-D` tunes
  the distances). A clip point moves in proportion to its attribute, so within one distance band
  a deepened strip stays planar, and a point two chunks share drops alike in both. Road chunks are shadow receivers only, so skirts
  cast no shadow.
- **Bridge fascias.** The bridge renderer emits a bridge span's fascias into the concrete layer and
  the slab from their bottom vertices row by row (`SpanPiece::strip_bottom_rows`), instead of its
  own `f32` section points: deck edge, fascia and slab share their vertices bitwise, mouth rows
  included (a node mouth's corner lies on the arm's offset curve, not on the section's lateral
  line, so the old slab ended a little off the deck there). The slab's payload changes (`f64`
  points, no `f32` world rounding before the chunk frame, a fascia-shared edge); no probe holds
  it. Piers are unchanged.
- **Product probe.** The node probe's seven top-surface hashes are unchanged for all 141
  entries (the strips are no part of the mesh the probe digests). Its new strip hash per
  fixture (`EXPECTED_STRIPS`, recorded by this gate: every entry is new) digests each piece's
  strip kind and every strip triangle's points and flags. The reference probe is unchanged.
- **Tests.** `strips_hang_from_the_outer_chains_bitwise` (all 141 probe fixtures: the kind per
  piece class, two triangles per chain segment, tops bitwise the chain positions, bottoms bitwise
  lowered, facing away from the road). `reference_junction_road_chunks_are_watertight` reads the
  skirt layer and is stricter: an edge with one face is open unless it is a skirt's bottom edge
  (both ends flagged bottom) under the footprint's edge (road 5 mm to one side, none to the
  other), so every outer edge of the top surface must be a skirt's top edge, bitwise (before, any
  one-face edge with no road across passed). `structure_and_rural_road_chunks_are_watertight` no
  longer exempts the whole concrete layer: only edges on a structure's free-end row, its mouth
  rows' concrete and vertical edges (the slab's and fascias' ends and the grounded skirts' ends
  there, which `TERRAIN-07-C`'s abutments and portals close) and a tunnel's sides (no strips;
  its bore is the portals'). The preview-equals-commit tests compare whole chunks, skirts
  included.
- **Payload packing (fresh, 2026-10-25, 17:33-17:34 EET, no restic).** Release library tests,
  `benchmark_road_preview_stages`, `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4`, `taskset -c 0,2,4,6,8,10,12,14`, both
  timing locks, C B B C C B B C in one session: C = `road` `6899d724` (this gate's base), B = the
  gate's sources, both built in one worktree and target directory (identities in `$ARTIFACTS`).
  Payload packing p50 ms, C runs / B runs: `sloped_t` 0.333, 0.334, 0.333, 0.332 / 0.385,
  0.391, 0.391, 0.384; `sloped_branch` 0.328, 0.329, 0.331, 0.334 / 0.381, 0.392, 0.385, 0.388
  (p95 at most 0.396 / 0.463). The stage grows by 0.055 ms (16-17%) with the skirts: 2,034 of
  B's 9,845 payload vertices per pose are skirt vertices on `sloped_t` (C's 7,811 grow by 26%)
  and 2,448 of 11,706 on `sloped_branch`, so a skirt vertex costs about 27 ns against C's 43 ns
  per payload vertex. Within the 1.0 ms budget (0.39 ms). Plan and roadbed are within C's spread
  (plan 0.467-0.472 / 0.467-0.471 and 0.407-0.412 / 0.407-0.418; roadbed 0.318-0.327 /
  0.321-0.329 and 0.322-0.326 / 0.321-0.326). The legacy terrain stage, whose code B does not
  change, sits up to 0.06 ms (1.3%) above C's range (4.591-4.610 / 4.606-4.671 and
  4.826-4.846 / 4.870-4.903); not profiled, so not attributed under
  [`roads.md` open question 36](roads.md#road-68-open-questions)'s rule; the stage is the exact
  cut that `TERRAIN-07-G` deletes.
- **Reference screenshots (fresh, 2026-10-25).** `road_junction_reference_test.gd` through
  `screenshots-C.sh` (gamescope headless, isolated profile), before (`6899d724` with this gate's

#### `TERRAIN-07-C` record

Round 1, 2026-10-26, branch `terrain07-C` from `road` at `5f2c5fbf` (gate A landed); items 1-3
and 5. Item 4 (structure ends) is round 2's, and the gate commit follows it. Fresh runs on this

**What landed.**

- Allocator (item 1): `SiteSource for BuildingAllocator`, the sites whose bounds meet a rectangle
  through the 512 m site chunks with their footprints, support heights and surfaces in authored
  order; it answers only while the chunk index is ready (`SiteSource::ready`), so the bake never
  scans the city (`BakeError::SitesUnavailable` otherwise). The allocator's footprint predicate is
  shared (`site_footprint_contains`). Every site change records a `SiteChange` (the site before or
  after it: the legacy box and its support height) in the same mutators as the legacy terrain
  boxes, into a second outbox that `SimCore`'s site publication moves to
  `last_site_terrain_changes` (`TERRAIN-07-E` consumes it).
- Graded (items 2, 3 and 5): `graded/sites.rs` (the window's sites in canonical order, `Pad`
  seams, the `Pad` class by the allocator's predicate, the material class of the first surface

**Speed-ups found on the way** (exact; the unpruned bake is their test): pads and surfaces take
the even-odd rule along each lattice row away from their sides and test the predicate only within
1 cm of a side or on a row within 1 cm of a corner (`for_each_span_point`); the allocator rules a
site out by its lot centre before reading its polygons; the walls' setters are found per 16 m
block of the tile's road seams, and the lattice surface is read only along seams with a walled
vertex. On the first build (`27fc85d90782`, same session, before them) the populated first edits
took 3.63-4.79 ms and the Kuopio edits a median 2.78 ms.

**What landed.**

- The exact lever 1 (`prune.rs` `listing_band`): pass 1 lists a pad seam only within its bind
  reach, never for the band, since no sample names a pad seam as its nearest; the bake's two
  passes and the selection's pass-1 test take every seam's band from that one function
  ([two passes](#the-grading-function)). The selection's floor reads the window's pad seams
  without the canonical site order and material edges (`SiteBuffer::gather_unordered`,
  `for_each_pad_seam`): a minimum is order-free, so the floor is the same bits.

  for review): a node piece where only bridges and tunnels meet is part of the structure
  (`NodeArms::grounded`): it hangs no skirt, and no grounded query, chain change or patch loop
  reads it (`PublishedPiece::grounded`), which closes `TERRAIN-07-B`'s skirt-in-the-air risk. A
  structure's free end (`is_structure_end`, the rule that gives it no node piece) is capped
  (`end_cap`): the polygon in the end row's vertical plane between the row and the bottoms below
  its corners (a bridge's fascia depth, so the cap's bottom is the slab's end edge; a tunnel's
  skirt depth, emitted in the skirt layer), triangulated by the roadbed's constrained ring
  triangulation in that plane, facing out of the span.

  bridges, a junction of tunnels, of bridges and a tunnel; a bend of a road and a bridge still
  grounded, flat and sloped); the strip probe checks the caps (end-row tops, corner bottoms,
  facing out) and re-records the 18 entries with a free structure end, every other strip entry
  and the seven top-surface hashes unchanged; `structure_and_rural_road_chunks_are_watertight`
  checks the free ends without an exception (the shared mouths keep theirs: the slab's and the

#### `TERRAIN-07-D` record

Round 1, 2026-10-26, branch `terrain07-D` from `road` at `5b138f8e` (gate C round 1 landed);
items 1-3. Items 4 and 5, the reference renders, the distance renders and the GPU idle-frame
matrix are round 2's; the gate commit follows them. Fresh runs on this branch.

**What landed.**

- Residency (item 1), `nodes/simulation_node/graded_tiles_api.rs`: Godot requests patch tile
  lists (`request_graded_patch_tiles`) and tile bakes by tile, level and `GL3` step
  (`request_graded_tiles`), each with a token it compares on arrival; one byte per request says
  whether it was queued (at most 96 tiles and 32 lists in flight, the bound on what Rust holds).
  The payload workers take a bounded snapshot under `try_lock` (the roadbed and the heightmap,
  whose chunks are shared, and the sites of the requested windows copied:
  `BuildingAllocator::graded_site_snapshot`, which answers inside its rectangles with the
  allocator's own filter, so the bake's bytes and inputs equal the live allocator's), bake off the
  lock with `bake_tiles`, one batch per level, and pack the slot bytes into pooled buffers.
  `poll_graded_tile_results` hands Godot at most the count it asks for; a busy core or an unready
  site index is retried, a representation error (`T7`) is not and is counted. Rust keeps no
  result once polled; eviction is Godot freeing the slot.
- Patch tile lists (item 2), `graded/residency.rs` `graded_tiles_in_rect`: from the bake's inputs
  (base, grounded seams and top triangles, sites within the cap), a tile is listed where some road
  or pad seam's cone can exclude the base over its part of the patch, a grounded top triangle
  meets it, or a site footprint or surface meets it. That is a superset of the tiles whose cells
  render differently from the base at any level, with no reach parameter: `g = max(L, min(b, U))`
  differs from `b` only where a cone excludes it. `O(P + S log S + S x tiles near each seam + T)`.
- Packing: `slot_side` (131, 67, 35 and, at `GL3`, `ceil(64 m / spacing) + 4`: 8 on 10 m cells at
  step 2), `slot_row_texels` (the seam row, then the material edges from the level's seam
  capacity) and `pack_slot` (little-endian RGBAF, the tile's lattice in the layer's lower corner).
- Godot (item 3): `terrain_graded_tiles.gd` (pools, residency, uploads, cells), the shader split
  into `terrain_surface.gdshaderinc` with the two thin variants `terrain.gdshader` (base, no
  discard) and `terrain_graded.gdshader` (`TERRAIN_GRADED`), and `terrain_cells.gdshaderinc`
  (lattices, stitching, clamping, the exact base, delta reads, the exact mask, the material
  class). Pools: per level a `Texture2DArray` for the texels and one for the rows, prewarmed at
  setup with 64, 192, 2,048 and 2,048 slots (`GL2` and `GL3` capped at the guaranteed array
  depth, [T23](#terrain-07-open-questions)): 18.4, 15.8, 50.6 and 10.5 MB, 95 MB in all on 10 m
  cells, with one pooled `Image` per level rewritten by `set_data` and uploaded by
  `update_layer`; an exhausted pool is counted and logged and leaves the tile as it was. Cells: per patch with graded tiles five `MultiMeshInstance3D` (the base cells
  and `GL0`-`GL3`), instance custom data `(tile x, slot, tile z, codes)`, identity transforms; the
  base cells share the patch's material through instance uniforms (`cell_mode`, the patch
  rectangle and the base lattice anchor), the PlaneMesh collapses while its cells draw, and the
  graded cells take one pooled graded material per patch, synced from the patch material when a
  watched parameter (height texture, masks, water, land cover, overlays) changes. Debug views
  `graded-delta`, `graded-sdf`, `graded-level` and `graded-slot` (`docs/debug.md`). The renderer
  is off by default (`terrain.gd` `graded_tiles_enabled`): the exact cut renders until round 2
  stops requesting refined patches (item 4), and stays renderable beside it for the reference
  comparison (T10).
- Rules fixed here: vertex positions are integer half-metres in the tile frame, the lattice codes
  (`GL0`-`GL2`, then the base lattice at `2^(code-3)` cells) order coarseness, and each side
  takes the coarser of its own and its neighbour's code, so the finer side snaps and the coarser
  one keeps its vertices; the base is `f32` bilinear over the patch heightmap's texels by
  `texelFetch` (exact on base lattice points), delta is the texel itself on lattice points (a
  `GL3` vertex clamped to a patch side off the step lattice interpolates between its two
  samples, the same on both patches); `GL3`'s step follows the tile's distance (2 to 5 km, 4 to
  12 km, 8 beyond), its cells draw with the step-2 mesh; a tile's token is the sum of the payload
  generations of the resident patches it meets. Shader integer division and remainder go through
  an exact floor division (GLSL leaves `%` undefined for negative operands).
- Correction recorded in the [query table](#queries-for-consumers): `normal_at` takes today's
  base gradient, as the shader does.

Round 2, 2026-10-26, the same branch rebased onto `road` at `74fe0a30`: the gate checks, item 4,
the coverage finding and the reference renders. Fresh runs on this branch.

- **GLES3 (fixed).** Two defects, both of the Compatibility renderer, found by probes of the
  shaders in isolation. (1) The graded variant's program with the base set's samplers plus the
  eight pool samplers failed to link ("too many fragment shader texture samplers"; four pool
  samplers link, six do not). Each graded level of a patch now draws with its own material, which
  binds that level's `graded_texels` and `graded_rows`, so a draw adds two samplers; the shader
  lost its per-level sampler switch and `CellFrame.level`. (2) The base cells drew nothing: the
  Compatibility renderer keeps `MultiMesh` instance custom data as half floats (14,043 arrives as
  14,040 or 14,048; Forward+ keeps it exact), which rounded the 15-bit lattice codes. Every
  channel is now an integer below 2,048: `x` the tile's column plus 32 times its row among the
  patch's tiles (from the tile holding the patch rectangle's lower corner, a patch spanning at most
  32 tiles), `y` the slot, `z` the codes' bits 0-8, `w` bits 9-14. Both variants link in both
  renderers, and `graded_cells_shader_test.gd` checks the base cell in the Compatibility renderer
  again.
- **Item 4 (done).** `terrain.gd` `graded_tiles_enabled` defaults on: every patch requests its
  plain payload (`_terrain_patch_payload_render_step_mm` returns 0) and no patch requires the
  engineered refinement, so the game never requests a refined CDT patch. Godot's
  `get_world_surface_height` and `intersect_world_surface` answer from `surface_height_at` and
  `raycast_surface` ([query table](#queries-for-consumers)). The exact cut stays reachable from
  `road_junction_reference_test.gd` only, which turns the switch off for its exact half (T10).
  Preview staging still shows the refined preview patches until `TERRAIN-07-E`.
- **The coverage finding (roadbed defect, for the coordinator).** Neither the top triangles nor
  the outer chains are wrong: the chains are the triangles' own vertices. The roadbed's
  point-in-triangle predicate (`top_triangle_height_at`, behind `height_at`) accepts points whose
  barycentric weights reach `-0.001`, so coverage extends up to 0.1% of a triangle's height past
  its edges. A probe without the 2 mm skip found one to three such points per fixture (480k
  points each, seven fixtures, `GL0` and `GL1`), every one within 1.3 mm of a chain and outside
  its covering triangle by exact orientation. Recorded in
  [`roads.md`, "Footprint and terrain"](roads.md#footprint-and-terrain) with the failing, ignored
  test `the_coverage_predicate_covers_no_point_outside_its_triangle` (3,662 of 3,822 edge probes
  on the T covered). The mask test now skips exactly the points the predicate covers outside every
  grounded top triangle (exact `orient2d`, at most a handful per fixture) and compares every other
  point bitwise; no distance tolerance remains.
- **Point query correction (taken 2026-10-26, confirmed by the user 2026-10-26; reversible in this
  branch).** With item 4, `./run.sh --test` failed `vehicle_ground_support_test.gd` ("buried
  contact", 16.1 mm of clearance against 19.8 mm) on a world without roads or sites: the vehicles
  stand on the bilinear base, and `ground_height_at` answered the `GL0` triangles of the base,
  whose chord lies 3.7 mm off the bilinear base at the fixture's grade breaks. `raycast_surface`
  already marched the bilinear base in tiles without a seam within the cap, so the two gate A
  queries disagreed there. `ground_height_at` now answers the bilinear base in such a tile too
  (the [query table](#queries-for-consumers) records the correction); every graded tile is
  unchanged, and the gate A query tests pass unchanged. Alternative: keep the `GL0` triangles
  everywhere and move the march and the vehicle contacts to them (the vehicles are `TERRAIN-07-F`'s).
- **Point query cost.** The query filled its base window over the whole cap window (about
  131 m square around the point), 17k samples per query on the 1 m grid of the vehicle fixture,
  which then ran past its 300 s timeout. It now fills one base cell around the rectangle it reads
  (a point's base reads only its four samples, so no value changes; the graded tests pass
  bitwise). The seam and site gathers still cover the cap; a gather variant for clustered points
  stays `TERRAIN-07-F`'s ([T19](#terrain-07-open-questions)).
- **`terrain_overlay_shader_test.gd` under Forward+** (pre-existing, `road` too): tracked as
  `TERRAIN-08` in the roadmap. The test reads its captures as linear light, which holds in the
  Compatibility renderer only; Forward+ captures are sRGB-encoded (0.726 measured against the
  linear 0.5). The test's capture decoding, not the terrain shader, so not fixed here.

- **Item 5 (built).** A commit bakes and installs its dirty resident tiles. The core journals
  each published edit (`nodes/sim/core/graded_edits.rs`): a roadbed install (commit or undo)
  with its terrain changes and `O(1)` snapshots of the heightmap and of the roadbed after it and
  at the previous install (an undo's restore swaps pieces before its install takes the changes,
  so the previous record's roadbed is its `before`), a site publication with its changes, a
  terrain brush's rectangle, and a world reset (every tile; also a journal past 64 edits). Each
  road or site record copies the sites within the selection's reach of its changed bounds
  (`selection_site_reach_m` at `GL2`, the widest the snapshot serves). Godot's residency poll
  takes the journal under `try_lock` (the first take starts it, so a core no graded renderer
  reads keeps nothing) and a payload worker runs each edit's selection at every level
  (`GradedEdit::select`): `dirty_tiles_for_road_changes` and `dirty_tiles_for_site_changes` with
  the edit's own snapshots at `GL0`-`GL2`, and at `GL3`, whose band reaches past the snapshot,
  with a site source that reads nothing, which drops the floor to `-inf` and selects a superset;
  `dirty_tiles_for_base_area` for a brush. Godot gives each dirty tile it holds at that level
  (installed or in flight) the edit's serial as its token, drops a bake in flight with an older
  token, and holds the rebaked results until every installed tile of the edit has one, then
  installs them in one frame; a tile at an unchanged level is rewritten into its own slot, so an
  edit needs no free slot and rewrites no instance. A tile's token no longer sums its resident
  patches' payload generations, which rebaked tiles whenever a neighbouring patch became
  resident, and a patch whose tile list is being refreshed keeps its last list (it dropped every
  tile of an edited patch until the new list arrived, so the base drew there for some frames).
  Preview adoption and the undo's kept tiles stay `TERRAIN-07-E`'s; an undo that resets the
  network render state journals a world reset.

- **The render defect (fixed at its cause).** Round 2's item 4 made Godot request every patch's
  plain payload (step 0), but Rust still refused a plain payload for a road-owned patch, the exact
  cut's contract (`terrain_patch_payload_build_source_for_request` returned no source when the
  patch required engineered refinement). The request came back as a retry, Godot asked again the
  next frame, and so on forever: no patch under a road installed, the terrain never settled, and
  the graded tiles (listed only by installed patches) never baked. It showed on the dummy
  renderer as well: on a 512 m world with the T, 12 of 16 patches installed and the 4 under the
  road stayed requested at step 0 for 300 frames, on the GPU too; round 3's "patches with no
  graded tile are missing too" was those views seeing only the road's patches. The plain payload
  is the patch's heightmap and is now served for every patch; the exact cut still asks road-owned
  patches at the refined step, so the reference test's exact half is unchanged. With the fix the
  same world settles in 10 frames on the GPU with every patch installed, 10 graded tiles and 4
  patches drawing cells. The Rust test that asserted the refusal
  (`raw_terrain_payload_is_rejected_for_road_locked_patch`) now asserts the plain payload
  (`plain_terrain_payload_is_served_for_road_locked_patch`). Regression check in the headless
  suite `./run.sh --test` runs: `graded_tile_renderer_test.gd` now also runs the production
  renderer (`terrain.gd`, graded on) over its roads and requires it to settle with every patch
  installed, the junction's patch included, and the junction's tile drawn graded; against the
  library without the fix it fails 8 assertions (0 patches installed), with it 0.
- **A refused request surfaces (built, the coordinator's follow-up).** The defect hid because a
  request Rust refused by contract came back as a retry and was asked again every frame. The
  build source now says why it has none (`PayloadDeferral`): a transient state Godot retries (a
  stale generation, a roadbed not yet current, a terrain stroke in progress) or a refusal by
  contract (today a patch outside the world). `poll_ready_terrain_patch_payloads` reports
  refusals apart (`refused_requests`, `refused_reasons`); `terrain.gd` logs each once on the
  `terrain` debug channel, never requests that patch at that step again and counts it
  (`get_pending_render_work_counts()["refused"]`), and `graded_tile_renderer_test.gd` fails on
  any (`a_request_outside_the_world_is_refused_not_retried` checks the Rust half).
- **Re-entrant scratch (fixed).** `kuopio_t2_wall`'s session aborted with "RefCell already
  borrowed": a payload worker held its thread-local bake scratch (and the edit selection's)
  borrowed across the bake's Rayon join, where it can steal another bake of the same kind. The
  scratch is now taken out of the thread-local for the call and put back after
  (`graded_tiles_api.rs` `with_scratch`).

  little-endian `f32` per face; `packed_walls_hold_the_faces_bitwise` checks every face of every
  fixture and level), and the renderer draws them as described in the
  [renderer rules](#godot-tile-renderer): one pooled, prewarmed `MultiMesh` of a quad per cell
  set, a face per instance in the patch holding its midpoint, placed by
  `terrain_graded_walls.gdshader` from its instance transform and lit through
  `standard_light.gdshaderinc`; nothing created per edit. The headless suite turns the T's side
  road into a bridge over a hollow and requires one instance per face (22 faces over 6 installed

- **"Too many instances using shader instance variables" (attributed; outside gate D).** Godot
  reserves 16 vec4 slots per instance whose material has instance uniforms; the default
  `rendering/limits/global_shader_variables/buffer_size` of 65,536 slots holds 4,096 such
  instances. The errors come only during the camera paths of the saved sessions, from the water
  reflection's tree impostor proxies (`water_reflection.gd` `_free_tree_proxies` 3,223 of 3,782,
  `_sync_proxy` 55), whose `vegetation_wind` material has an instance uniform, as do the trees
  they mirror; the `instance_buffer_pos` errors are later allocations of instances whose first one
  failed (Godot keeps the failed position). Capacity, both modes; graded adds its cell
  `MultiMesh`es (the cells' instance uniforms), hence 4,181-4,535 errors against 3,782-3,808. The
  levers (a larger buffer, or proxies without instance uniforms) are the water reflection's and
  vegetation's, for the coordinator: tracked as [`WATER-05`](roadmap.md#validated-bugs) (round 6).

  (a `GL0` layer of 275 KB and its rows) is the frame's largest step. Recommended: check the
  budget before each tile's upload and keep the tiles polled but not yet uploaded in a queue that
  the next frame installs first (Rust hands a result over once, so a polled tile cannot stay
  there); a frame then ends within the budget plus one tile's upload, `O(1)` per tile.

#### `TERRAIN-07-E` — preview, commit, undo and load

1. The terrain half of `preview_road` bakes graded tiles in place of refined patches; Godot stages
   them by slot swap.
2. Preview poses that bake only the tiles whose inputs changed since the last pose; commit
   adoption of the last pose's tiles by inputs; undo and redo by swapping the kept tiles back
   ([T20](#terrain-07-open-questions) (a)); load by residency.
3. The commit's terrain validation is removed: no terrain failure can reject a road.

- preview tile data equals the committed tile data, a fresh bake and the tiles after save and load,
  bitwise, in Rust tests over the T, Y, four-way, a split trunk and their sloped variants, and in

  from gate C on 2026-10-26 under T20 (a), for review: their full-edit bakes take 2.85-4.10 ms
  on four workers, gate C's evidence), replayed as drags: each pose's delta and the commit's
  adoption at most 3.0 ms on four workers, with T21's exact levers (a), among them a tile's rows

#### `TERRAIN-07-E` record

Round 1, 2026-10-26, branch `terrain07-E` from `road` at `bcf865a2` (`ROAD-68-K23`'s exact
coverage predicate landed). The Rust half; the Godot half (item 1's slot-swap staging,
`road_junction_preview_test.gd`, the Godot install share, the idle-clock preview stream) waits
for `TERRAIN-07-D` to land on `road`. Fresh runs on this branch, kept apart from earlier gates'.

**What landed.**

- Staging (`graded/stage.rs`): a `TileStage` holds baked tiles in `(level, tile)` order with
  shared payloads; `stage_tiles` is the one rule of poses, commit and undo ([corrections
  above](#preview-commit-undo-and-load)); `tile_inputs` and `gather_inputs` (`graded/tile.rs`)
  gather a bake's inputs through the bake's own gathers and assembly without sampling; the
  payloads of stages no longer held are reused once nothing shares them (`StageScratch::retire`).
  `Level` is ordered, finest first.
- Preview (`nodes/sim/core/graded_stage.rs`): each pose selects the dirty tiles of the pose's
  roadbed against the published one at `GL0` and stages them against the last pose's tiles
  (`RoadPreviewContext::graded`), on `RoadPreviewPieces::graded`, `RoadPreviewTimes::graded_ms`
  and the preview dictionary (`graded_ms`, `graded_adopted`, `graded_baked`). The pose reads the
  sites through the view's per-patch site snapshots (`RoadTerrainInputs`), answered with the
  allocator's own test (the lot centre within the largest lot radius, then the bounds; both now
  captured with each snapshot) and deduplicated by content, so the inputs are the allocator's.
- Commit: stages its dirty tiles over the live roadbed, sites and terrain against the current
  preview's tiles (`SimCore::last_graded_tiles` and `last_graded_stats`, the metrics
  `surface_graded_ms` and `graded_*`, also in the commit breakdown's records); a preview with a
  stale fingerprint offers none. Its undo record keeps the replaced tiles, baked by a pure job
  after the commit from the pre-commit roadbed and heightmap (`O(1)`) and a copy of the sites of
  the tiles' windows (`BuildingAllocator::graded_site_snapshot`, `TERRAIN-07-D`'s `SiteSnapshot`,
  ported unchanged); benchmark mode keeps no undo record and spawns no job.
- Undo publishes the restored roadbed, selects the restore's dirty tiles and stages them against
  the kept tiles (`SimCore::restage_graded_tiles_for_undo`).
- Item 3: the commit's terrain validation is removed with what only it used (the exact cut's
  build and preview adoption at the commit, `RefinedTerrainRestore` and the undo record's
  refined entries, the preview patches' source signatures, `preview_terrain_adopted`,
  `surface_terrain_ms`). The exact cut's synchronous patch build remains for the commit
  breakdown's fixture and the exact cut's tests (`build_road_terrain_patches`, test builds
  only); the preview still builds the exact cut's patches for Godot's preview until the Godot
  half replaces them with graded tiles.
- The terrain-edit refusal (`roads.md` question 37, K15 (1), and question 48, closed):
  authoritative terrain undo (a terrain record keeps the source terrain; undo restores the
  source and the visual buffer from it) and the rollback of a stroke whose sync leaves a road
  steeper than 1:3 and steeper than before.
- Tests: `gathered_inputs_are_the_bakes_and_a_stage_adopts_by_inputs`,
  `graded_tiles_of_drags_commits_undo_and_loads_equal_fresh_bakes`,
  `a_stale_context_commit_bakes_and_equals_a_fresh_bake`,
  `a_terrain_edit_that_steepens_a_road_past_one_in_three_is_refused`; converted: the two
  rollback tests refuse their commit with a field under the new road instead of a terrain
  failure (`planned_topology_rejection_restores_split_dependents`,
  `rejected_commit_restores_split_dependents_and_preserves_undo_history`),
  `accepted_road_has_its_graded_tiles_before_publication`, the trunk-branch and split-trunk
